paragraphs: Abba bar Acha—[Berakhot 25b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.25b.5); Rav Ada bar Acha—[Zevachim 22a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.22a.2); Rav Huna bar Acha—[Yerushalmi Maaser Sheni 5:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Maaser_Sheni.5.5.8); Rav Chuna bar Acha—[Sukkah 52b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.52b.7); Rabbi Yaakov, son of Rav Acha—Moed Katan 27b[^2]; Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha—[Berakhot 23a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.23a.17); Rav Yirmeyah bar Acha—[Chullin 51b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.51b.9); Rav Mesharshiya, son of Rav Acha—[Chullin 67b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.67b.12); Rav Shmuel bar Acha—[Nazir 51b](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.51b.3).[^1]

notes.text: Berakhot 25b gives the longer name Rabbi Acha bar Abba bar Acha as an alternative attribution. Sukkah calls the reporter Rav Chana bar Acha. The Yerushalmi names Rabbi Huna bar Acha and gives Rabbi Alexandri as his authority. The list groups the name forms across separate notices.

At [Moed Katan 27a:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.27a.15), the name is Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha. He gives rulings in the names of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi and Rabbi Assi. Hyman cites 27b here and gives his father the title Rav.
